Appendix, speaker only. Pre-flight, from runbook §4. Do one full cold bring-up before the audience arrives; never time it for the first time on stage. Run from the aip-demo repo root.

T-60 (once per clone):
cp .env.template .env   # edit .env: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is REQUIRED
uv venv --python 3.13 .venv && uv pip install -r tests/requirements.txt && .venv/bin/playwright install chromium
for svc in tools/payments-mcp agents/settlement-agent agents/claims-agent platform/policy-decision-service apps/reviewer-ui platform/eval-scorer; do (cd "$svc" && uv venv --python 3.13 .venv && uv pip install -r requirements.txt); done
(cd platform/policy-decision-service && ./gen-stubs.sh)
Never install into an existing service venv; delete and recreate it.

T-30:
./scripts/setup-kind.sh --stage 7
Stage 7 is stage 6 plus Kyverno and the keystone policy; step 4 needs it.
Check at the end: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: SET. If it says EMPTY, stop: every pod comes up Running and the first claim fails at the model call. Every component installed, no rollout timeouts.

T-15:
./scripts/start-demo.sh
It owns every port-forward; Ctrl+C stops them all. Leave that terminal alone. Confirm a Backstage line, not "Backstage: SKIPPED".

T-10, with your own eyes:
kubectl get pods -A --no-headers | wc -l
kubectl get pods -A --no-headers | grep -v ' Running \| Completed ' || echo "all Running"
Kyverno Ready, and the keystone policy in place:
kubectl -n kyverno get pods
kubectl get validatingpolicy agents-cannot-edit-their-own-authority
  If Kyverno is not Ready, stop and fix it before step 4. Also check its webhook is registered (kubectl get validatingwebhookconfiguration kyverno-resource-validating-webhook-cfg -o jsonpath='{.webhooks[*].name}' (expect vpol.validate.kyverno.svc-fail-finegrained-agents-cannot-edit-their-own-authority; ./scripts/start-demo.sh checks it for you)): a gracefully stopped Kyverno deletes its own webhooks, and the keystone is then off without a word.
The over-grant is absent:
kubectl get -f deploy/demo/keystone-overgrant.yaml
  expect: NotFound for both objects. If it exists, delete it: kubectl delete -f deploy/demo/keystone-overgrant.yaml
kubectl -n northstar-platform get featureflag northstar-autonomy -o jsonpath='{.spec.flagSpec.flags.autonomy-level.state}{"  default="}{.spec.flagSpec.flags.autonomy-level.defaultVariant}{"\n"}'
  expect: ENABLED  default=assisted
TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST localhost:7007/api/auth/guest/refresh | python3 -c 'import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["backstageIdentity"]["token"])')
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" localhost:7007/api/autonomy-contract/status | python3 -m json.tool
  expect: state ENABLED, defaultVariant assisted, and perIdentity settlement-agent = assisted (targeting-then). A bare curl without the token gets HTTP 401 Missing credentials: that is expected.
Then the five checks in the browser: customer UI http://localhost:8080; reviewer UI http://localhost:8081; Jaeger http://localhost:16686 with its service dropdown populated; Backstage http://localhost:7007 with Guest → Enter working; the Autonomy contract card reading assisted / assisted.

No open approvals:
curl -s localhost:8081/api/awaiting
expect: []

T-5, the rehearsal claim:
./scripts/demo claim 5800 --expect awaiting_approval
./scripts/demo approve last
It exits non-zero unless the claim waits for a human. One model call; it proves the API key, the A2A chain, the gateway, the PDS, flagd, the ledger and the reviewer-ui. Then, as the last thing before the audience sees anything:
./scripts/demo reset
It rejects any open approval as demo-reset, puts the flag back to assisted, checks flagd, deletes any over-grant, clears the run state, and prints what it verified.

Source: aip-demo docs/demo-runbook.md §4; M7 design spec §2.1, §2.2, §4

KASPER

Appendix, speaker only. Reset between runs, from runbook §7. This is the checklist that matters most.

One command does items 1 and 3, and rejects any open approval as demo-reset. It is the first thing to type when something looks off:
./scripts/demo reset
It is idempotent and prints what it verified (open approvals, over-grant, flag). Run it at the end of every rehearsal and every performance. The manual checks below are what it automates.

1. The contract must be left refusing. Check:
kubectl -n northstar-platform get featureflag northstar-autonomy -o jsonpath='{.spec.flagSpec.flags.autonomy-level.targeting}{"\n"}'
Both branches must read "assisted". If it is flipped, flip it back through the Backstage card, http://localhost:7007/autonomy-contract → "Set settlement-agent: assisted", so the revert gets its own audit span. Or:
kubectl -n northstar-platform apply -f deploy/platform/openfeature/featureflag.yaml
A cluster left autonomous settles 5,800 euros without a human, and step 2 collapses.

2. The ledger is per-process and in memory. Restart payments-api to clear old rows from the reviewer UI:
kubectl -n northstar-systems rollout restart deploy/payments-api

3. The over-grant is gone. Step 4 (demo keystone) applies a Role and RoleBinding that let settlement-agent patch its own flag, then deletes them. If the script stopped halfway, they are still there. Check:
kubectl get -f deploy/demo/keystone-overgrant.yaml
Expect NotFound for both. If not: kubectl delete -f deploy/demo/keystone-overgrant.yaml
Left behind, the agent holds a standing grant to edit its own authority, and only Kyverno stands in the way.

4. Payment ids are cumulative since that pod's last restart, so PAY-000001 only appears on a fresh one. Never promise a specific payment id on stage.

Source: aip-demo docs/demo-runbook.md §7; M7 design spec §2.2

KASPER

Appendix, speaker only. Live triage, from runbook §8. Symptom, likely cause, fix:

- First claim submission errors: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY empty. It is a model call. Check .env, restart the agent deployments.
- A surface at 5601 / 9090 / 7007 doesn't answer: dead port-forward (a dead forward keeps its socket bound and still looks healthy to lsof). Ctrl+C and re-run ./scripts/start-demo.sh. Kind host ports (8080, 8081, 16686) survive a redeploy; the port-forwards don't.
- "Backstage: SKIPPED" in start-demo output: cluster below stage 6. ./scripts/setup-kind.sh --stage 7 (no recreate needed from stage 3+).
- 5,800 euros settles at the start of step 2: contract left flipped from a previous run. ./scripts/demo reset, then re-run the step.
- The customer tab never flips to Settled: check the claims-agent forward in ./scripts/start-demo.sh, then run ./scripts/demo approve last. If the money moved but the claim was never told (the command prints that it could not tell the claim), run the same command again: the reviewer-ui sees the decision is already on the ledger, moves no money, and tells the claim again. It finds the claim from the ledger even after it has left the reviewer's queue. The payment is settled either way.
- A claims-agent restart while a claim waits: waiting tasks live in its memory, by design. ./scripts/demo reset rejects them; file the claim again.
- scripts/demo prints FAIL: the expected outcome did not happen; that is the command doing its job. Read the line, ./scripts/demo reset, re-run the one step.
- 5,800 euros waits at autonomous: the flag did not take, or the caller identity is wrong. Check the card; check northstar.policy.caller.spiffe_id on the span.
- Backstage card shows the old value: it reads live, so the write failed. Check the response, then kubectl -n northstar-platform get featureflag northstar-autonomy as an independent witness.
- Step 4 (demo keystone) says 'patched' instead of Denied: the keystone is OFF. Kyverno was stopped gracefully and deleted its own webhooks on the way out (measured 2026-10-12). kubectl -n kyverno get pods; restart it, wait for the vpol webhook to reappear, re-run the step. Backstage's flip is never affected by a Kyverno outage: the policy's identity match is evaluated by the API server before the webhook is called.
- Step 4 fails with 'failed calling webhook ... connection refused': Kyverno is registered but unreachable, so agent writes fail closed. That is the safe failure; restart Kyverno.
- Jaeger shows two disconnected traces: trace context broken at a hop. Expected only for the human approval, which is a link by design (the longer demo's beat 4).
- Scores come back with spanCount still climbing: OpenSearch near-real-time lag. Wait, re-ask with "emit": false until it settles.
- A pod is CrashLooping: kubectl -n <ns> logs <pod> --previous

Two things to know about, not to fix live:
- Trace A is huge and still growing while a claim waits: the agent SDK adds a polling span about every half second. Expected and kept; open it after the decision, or use the terminal's trace view.
- A NoTaskQueue ERROR in the claims-agent log after an approve: the SDK's cleanup on every resume. Expected noise; the claim completed.
- The reviewer-ui has no ingress policy and no login: any pod with egress to it can approve. Out of scope for this demo; say so plainly if asked.

Never do these live:
- ./scripts/teardown.sh destroys the cluster and the local registry. A rebuild is not a five-minute operation.
- ./scripts/smoke-test.sh is the full gate: it spends model tokens, drives browsers, and takes about 10 minutes. Use the T-10 checks instead.

Source: aip-demo docs/demo-runbook.md §8, §6; M7 design spec §2.1 (failurePolicy: Fail)
